short_description: Husfeld et al. (1989) NLTE H-He atmospheres for hot helium-rich stars, Teff 35-80 kK (SVO Husfeld)
description: SVO's "Husfeld et al models for non-LTE Helium-rich stars": NLTE hydrogen-helium model atmospheres (Husfeld, Butler, Heber & Drilling 1989), Teff 35,000-80,000 K, log g 4.0-7.0, helium abundance Y(He) 0, 0.01, 0.10, 0.25, 0.35, 0.50 and 0.70. There is no metallicity axis: each Y(He) value is a variant with its own MESA cube.

default_variant_note: Since 25 Nov 2026 the grid has no top-level flux_cube.bin: its top-level flux_cube_nd.bin is the all-axes cube (Teff, log g and Y(He)) of every variant, and MESA colors reads the per-variant folders Husfeld_yhe_0p00 to Husfeld_yhe_0p70, each with its own flux_cube.bin and lookup table. The default variant is the one NJM's grid comparison tables (grid_info.compare) use when Husfeld is named without a variant. From 29 Oct to 25 Nov 2026 the top-level flux_cube.bin was a byte copy of this variant's cube; the one served before 29 Oct 2026 was empty. Y(He) = 0.10 is a choice, not a fact of the grid: it is the value nearest the solar helium abundance by number (about 0.09), but SVO's page says only 'value for the Helium abundance', not whether Y(He) is a number or a mass fraction (by mass the nearest would be 0.25). Nill to confirm.

repairs.decision: Niall Miller, 27 Nov 2026: set tiny negatives to 0, repair the two
repairs.why: SVO's Husfeld files (identical to NJM's copy, value for value, checked 2026-11-25) hold negative fluxes, which an emergent flux cannot have. No publisher documentation explaining them was found.

rule.numerical_zero: negative with |F| <= 2.220446e-16 * max|F| of the spectrum: set to 0
rule.significant: window of samples negative or off by more than 1% from the interpolation between the nearest valid neighbours along the first of ['yhe', 'logg', 'teff'] that has them: replaced by that interpolation

numerical_zeros.threshold: float64 machine epsilon (2.2e-16) times the spectrum's largest |flux|: a value below it is beneath the spectrum's own floating-point resolution. These values are at most 1.5e-40 of their spectrum's peak; the Paschen alpha negatives are 5.0e-7 to 4.0e-5 of theirs.

repairs.note: Both windows are a sign-flipping oscillation in the Paschen alpha line core (18,751 A) of a single model; every grid neighbour has a smooth positive emission bump there. The window is the run of samples around the negatives that are negative or differ by more than 1 % from the interpolation between the model's two Y(He) neighbours, and it is replaced by that interpolation.
not_repaired: Husfeld_fid211.txt (55,000 K, log g 5.0, Y(He) 0): its Paschen alpha core is flat-topped at 2.46 times the continuum, against 1.33-1.47 in its neighbours, but it holds no negative flux; left as published
Husfeld_fid164.txt: a single-sample positive spike at 4,860.52 A (H beta), about 2.1 times the expected value, not next to any negative sample; left as published
